questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: What does the Italian word "fiume" mean in English?
questions.explanation: The Italian word "fiume" is a place noun that translates into English as "river". Nouns in Italian also carry grammatical gender, here masculine, a feature English nouns do not mark.
questions.hint: Think of the place word family when recalling "fiume".

options.misconception: this is the tu form of the verb, not lui/lei
this is the io form of the verb, not lui/lei

questions.explanation: The future form of "arrivare" for "lui/lei" is "arrivarà". The future tense is built on the infinitive stem, with endings that mark each person. It expresses an action that has not yet happened. Selecting the wrong person ending changes who performs the action.
questions.hint: Identify the subject pronoun, then apply the future ending for that person.

questions.stem: Which indefinite article precedes "insegnante"?
questions.explanation: The noun "insegnante" is masculine and begins with a vowel, so the indefinite article is "un". Italian changes the indefinite article for gender and for vowel-initial words.
questions.hint: Match the article to both the gender and the first sound of the noun.
